name: Atmospheric CO₂
summary: CO₂ 428.65 ppm at Mauna Loa in the week of 8 Nov, up 2.35 ppm on a year, inside the 2–3 ppm Watch band
state: Mauna Loa recorded 428.65 ppm in the week of 8 Nov, 2.35 ppm higher than a year earlier and inside the 2.0–3.0 ppm Watch band (NOAA GML). Weekly growth figures are noisy; the week before showed growth above 3 ppm. El Niño years tend to bring faster CO₂ growth as tropical land absorbs less carbon.
for_you: CO₂ growth is a long-run climate driver rather than a near-term hazard; it shapes the pace of warming over coming decades.
rubric_hit: CO₂ y/y +2.35 ppm within 2.0–3.0 Watch band

sources.title: NOAA GML — Trends in atmospheric CO₂ (Mauna Loa)

why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.
